fields.Name: Stripe
fields.Description: Stripe payments — cards, wallets, hosted checkout.

_comments: Stripe ACH (US bank debit) — a SEPARATE type from 'Stripe', deliberately.
The two rails are different money. They settle on different timescales (instant against up to
four business days), cost different amounts (2.9% + 30c against 0.8% capped at $5), and — the
one that actually shapes the code — a bank debit can be TAKEN BACK after it has been booked.
Folding them into one provider row would mean an operator could not enable one without the
other, and every fee expectation in the system would have to branch on the instrument rather
SupportsTokenization is 1 because the instrument a debit charges IS a saved payment method —
collected once through a Stripe SetupIntent, along with the NACHA authorisation Stripe retains
against it. This driver never collects one; it charges one that already exists.
SupportsRefund is 1 for a DELIBERATE refund (Orders.RefundPayment). A bank RETURN is a
different thing and does not go through the refund path — it arrives as a webhook and

fields.Name: Stripe ACH
fields.Description: Stripe US bank debits (ACH). Settles on the bank's schedule rather than at the till: a payment is captured by the webhook when the debit clears, and a debit RETURNED after settlement is reversed by a new payment rather than by editing the original. 0.8% capped at $5.

fields.Name: Manual
fields.Description: Finance records the money movement by hand (check, wire, cash). Always available.

fields.Name: Stored Value
fields.Description: Money we already hold: a gift card (StoredValueAccount, a bearer instrument with a redeemable code) or an over-paid order's negative balance (account credit, D68). One driver, because the mechanics of spending them are identical even though their ownership, transferability, expiry and accounting treatment are not. No gateway — we are the institution, so there is no fee.

fields.Name: J.P. Morgan
fields.Description: PLACEHOLDER, deliberately INACTIVE. Which API is an open question — legacy Orbital/Paymentech versus the newer J.P. Morgan Payments API — and the answer changes the driver, not just its credentials. The row exists so the type is addressable and the capability flags are somewhere to correct; activating it before a driver is registered would make PaymentProviderResolver refuse, which is the correct behaviour and a confusing way to discover this.
